analysis.investment_thesis: Carborundum Universal is a quality industrial franchise with a clean balance sheet, but at 74x trailing P/E on sharply declining profits it is priced for perfection in a business that delivered only 10.8% revenue CAGR over nine years. The 37% collapse in net profit (FY24: ₹476 Cr → FY25: ₹299 Cr) and near-zero FCF of ₹28 Cr in FY25 make the current valuation indefensible.
key_strengths: Near debt-free balance sheet (D/E 0.08) with ₹378 Cr cash, giving financial resilience through cycles
Diversified three-segment model (abrasives, technical ceramics, electrominerals) with long operating history since 1954
Strong DII confidence (30% holding) signals institutional conviction in the franchise
key_risks: Valuation is extreme: 74x trailing P/E for a business growing revenue at ~10% CAGR and ROE of only 10.8% — far below my 15% minimum threshold
Profit destruction in FY25 — net profit fell 37% YoY and other income swung from +₹118 Cr to -₹23 Cr, suggesting one-off hits or deteriorating subsidiaries
Free cash flow near collapse — OCF of ₹304 Cr against capex of ₹278 Cr leaves only ₹28 Cr FCF; prior year was ₹367 Cr FCF
red_flags: Net profit declined 37% in FY25 (₹476 Cr → ₹299 Cr) while market still values at 74x — dangerous combination
Promoter holding only 38.9%, below my comfort threshold of 50%; no strong promoter conviction visible
Other income turned sharply negative (-₹23 Cr in FY25 vs +₹136 Cr in FY23) suggesting subsidiary losses or asset write-downs masking operational picture
analysis.detailed_analysis:
CRISIL-grade industrial business with a 70-year history in abrasives and ceramics, but the financial trajectory in FY25 is alarming. Revenue grew only 4% YoY (₹4,702 Cr → ₹4,894 Cr), EBITDA fell from ₹864 Cr to ₹805 Cr, and net profit crashed 37%. The negative other income (-₹23 Cr) is particularly worrying and may signal subsidiary write-offs. ROCE of 16% is decent but ROE of 10.8% for an industrial is unimpressive, and the business does not earn its cost of capital at current valuations.

From my philosophy, I want businesses growing 15-25% with ROE above 20% at 20-30x P/E for high-quality compounders. CARBORUNIV fails on growth rate, ROE, and — most critically — current year profit trajectory. The forward P/E of ~39x assumes a dramatic profit recovery in FY26 that is far from certain. I would wait for either a 40-50% price correction or sustained earnings recovery before revisiting.
